nom.title: Nominative
nom.explanation: The plain, undecorated form of a noun — the subject of a sentence, and the form a dictionary lists. Every other entry in this reference adds something to this base form.

acc.title: Accusative
acc.suffix: -t (with a linking vowel — -at/-et/-ot/-öt — after most consonant-final stems)
acc.explanation: Marks the direct object: whatever an action is done to. Because this suffix, not word order, says who does what to what, Hungarian word order is free to shift for emphasis instead.

dat.title: Dative
dat.explanation: Marks who or what something is given, said, or done for. Hungarian also reuses it to say "have" — paired with van/nincs, since there's no separate verb for "to have".

ins.title: Instrumental-comitative
ins.suffix: -val / -vel (the v assimilates to double the stem's final consonant: ház -> házzal, not házval)
ins.explanation: Covers both senses English keeps separate: the tool or means something is done with, and the company someone is with.

cfi.title: Causal-final
cfi.explanation: Expresses a reason, a goal, or an exchange — what something is done for, or traded for.

tra.title: Translative
tra.explanation: Marks a change of state — becoming or turning into something.

ter.title: Terminative
ter.explanation: Marks an endpoint — up to or until, whether in time or in space.

esf.title: Essive-formal
esf.explanation: In the role or capacity of something — English's "as a...".

esm.title: Essive-modal
esm.explanation: Describes how something is done — especially the language something is done in.

ine.title: Inessive
ine.explanation: Static location: inside something, at rest.

example.en: The book is in the bag.

sup.title: Superessive
sup.explanation: Static location: on top of a surface, at rest.

example.en: The key is on the table.

ade.title: Adessive
ade.explanation: Static location: near, at, or "at someone's place" — the closest Hungarian gets to French chez.

ill.title: Illative
ill.explanation: Motion into the inside of something.

sub.title: Sublative
sub.explanation: Motion onto the top of a surface.

example.en: I'm putting the book onto the table.

all.title: Allative
all.explanation: Motion toward or up to near someone or something — arriving at, not necessarily inside.

example.en: I'm going to my friend's place.

ela.title: Elative
ela.explanation: Motion out of the inside of something — the reverse of the inessive/illative pair.

example.en: I'm coming out of the room.

del.title: Delative
del.explanation: Motion off a surface — and, just as often in everyday speech, "about" a topic.

abl.title: Ablative
abl.explanation: Motion away from near someone or something (not out of — just away from the vicinity). Also used for "from" a person, and in comparisons ("than").

example.en: I got a present from my mom.

plural.title: Plural
plural.suffix: -k (with a linking vowel — -ak/-ek/-ok/-ök — after most consonant-final stems)
plural.explanation: Marks more than one. Attaches directly to the bare noun, before any case suffix — a noun is always made plural first, then put into its case (barát -> barátok -> barátoknak, "friend" -> "friends" -> "to the friends").

possessive.title: Possessive
possessive.explanation: Hungarian marks "my/your/his/her/our/your/their" directly on the possessed noun itself, rather than with a separate possessive pronoun the way English does — a bit like English's "'s", but for every person, not just the third.
